governing_codes.title: Eurocode 8: Design of structures for earthquake resistance – Part 1
governing_codes.note: Provides the anchorage design framework for non-structural elements. Gives no brace spacing or clearance dimensions for MEP distribution systems. None of this config's thresholds come from it.

governing_codes.title: German National Annex to EN 1998-1 – nationally determined parameters
governing_codes.note: Governs in Germany. Gives no MEP brace spacing or clearance dimensions. DIN 4149:2005-04 was withdrawn and replaced by DIN EN 1998-1:2010-12 with its National Annex; it is historical only.

governing_codes.title: Reducing the Risks of Nonstructural Earthquake Damage – A Practical Guide
governing_codes.note: Source of the dimensional logic where a threshold is marked sourced. A guide, not a code.

governing_codes.title: Minimum Design Loads for Buildings and Other Structures
governing_codes.note: What FEMA E-74 defers to for the actual requirements. Cited as the upstream reference; not held.

governing_codes.title: Earthquake-resistant design of MEP supports, MT System – Hilti Corporation, document W4571 EN, 05/2022
governing_codes.relevant_clause: Annex A, "Tilt angle – for all bracings" (45° ± 15°); worked example §2.4.3; sprinkler pipe restraint spacing, citing NFPA 13 / EN 12845 Annex E (transverse 12 m / longitudinal 24 m)
governing_codes.note: A vendor design manual applying EN 1998-1 to MEP supports, not a code. It is the source of angle_constraints and, via its NFPA 13 / EN 12845 Annex E citation, of brace_types[*].spacing_transverse_m and spacing_longitudinal_m. It states the brace tilt angle on the horizontal level, the same datum this config uses. NFPA 13-based product literature (Eaton, nVent, Hilti US anchor load tables) measures brace angle from vertical instead and tabulates 30-90 degrees from vertical; that convention is not used here.

data_gaps: Thresholds marked status=authored in the provenance block are BIMGUARD screening calibration, not values stated by any standard held.
Brace spacing values describe piping; no source held gives a duct brace spacing.
seismic_parameters.hazard_factor_default is not set; left null.
brace_types[*].base_footprint_mm values are generic bracing-hardware footprint placeholders, not sourced; brace_types[*].standard_sizes are left empty pending a hardware catalogue cross-reference.
All four brace_types variants share the same spacing and clearance values; no source held distinguishes them.
At schema 1.1.0 no SB-001 code path reads seismic_parameters.importance_factors or thresholds.duct_area_sqm; both are recorded for provenance and future use.

changes: Replaced the brace spacing constants with values stated by a held source. brace_types.*.spacing_transverse_m 1.0 -> 12.0, spacing_longitudinal_m 1.5 -> 24.0 (metres).

Source: Hilti Seismic Manual, Earthquake-resistant design of MEP supports, MT System (05/2022), citing NFPA 13 / EN 12845 Annex E, sprinkler pipe restraint spacing 12 m transverse / 24 m longitudinal.

Both spacing thresholds are now status=sourced (were status=authored). The prior 1.0 m / 1.5 m values and their 'BIMGUARD authored calibration' label were inaccurate: per docs/planning/sb001_spacing_investigation.md (D:/claude-workspace/hilti-seismic), the values are the same unverified Hermes research pass that produced the fabricated brace angle, compounded by a feet-written-as-inches unit error. The Hermes summary's invented "NFPA 13-2021" entry read "40 in (transverse), 60 in (longitudinal)" and its invented "EN 1998-1:2020" entry read "1.0 m (transverse), 1.5 m (longitudinal)" -- the same two figures, one in each unit system, with the longitudinal value also carrying a digit change (80 -> 60) before being written in inches. hermes_config_expanded.py's min() merge then kept the smaller (EN) pair as-is. The real NFPA 13 figure the corrupted "40" belongs to is 40 ft transverse / 80 ft longitudinal (12.19 m / 24.38 m), which the Hilti Seismic Manual reports directly as 12 m / 24 m.

Cross-checked thresholds.pipe_diameter_mm (63.0, introduced in the same commit as the fabricated angle and spacing) against the same unit-mirroring signature: EN 63 mm = 2.48 in approx-equals NFPA's reported "2.5 in", the same pattern as the spacing values. No source held in the hilti-seismic corpus states a pipe-diameter seismic-bracing exemption threshold (NFPA 13, UFGS 23 05 48.19 and the Hilti Seismic Manual were searched; none give one), so the value is left unchanged at 63.0 but its status is corrected from authored to unsourced: it was never a BIMGUARD screening choice, it is the unverified Hermes figure with no available sourced replacement.

No SB-001 code path evaluates spacing_transverse_m, spacing_longitudinal_m or pipe_diameter_mm for a modelled brace at this commit beyond the SB-001.01/.03/.04 seeded numeric-comparison rules; halo_volume_generator.load_clearance_config reads all three into ClearanceRule. No current finding's severity or band changes as a result of this correction; only the values and their provenance change.
provenance_summary updated: 9 sourced, 0 derived, 4 authored, 1 unsourced (was 7 / 0 / 7).

Replaced the brace angle constraints with values stated by a held source. angle_constraints.min_degrees 40.0 -> 30.0, max_degrees 65.0 -> 60.0, ideal_degrees 52.5 -> 45.0, tolerance_degrees 12.5 -> 15.0. The datum is unchanged: degrees from horizontal, which is the convention the source uses.

Source: Hilti Seismic Manual, Earthquake-resistant design of MEP supports, MT System (05/2022), Annex A "Tilt angle – for all bracings", nominal 45° ± 15°, repeated on the typical application sheets and used in the worked example (§2.4.3, "Assuming α = 45°").

All four angle thresholds are now status=sourced. They were previously status=authored (min/max) and status=derived (ideal/tolerance), and the 40-65 range was labelled BIMGUARD authored calibration. That label was inaccurate: the 40-65 range was not authored by BIMGUARD. It was the surviving output of an unverified AI-assisted research summary (docs/validation/data/hermes_standards_research_summary.json), whose invented "DIN 4149:2022-03" entry read "40-65 degrees from horizontal" and whose invented "EN 1998-1:2020" entry read "35-70 degrees"; hermes_config_expanded.py intersected the two and computed 52.5/12.5 as the midpoint and half-range.

No SB-001 code path evaluates a modelled brace angle at this commit: phase_6d_seismic.py never reads angle_constraints, and clearance findings are unaffected. The values are consumed by load_clearance_config (ClearanceRule.angle_in_range), by the seeded rule row SB-001.05 and by scripts/validate_blue_halo.py. No current finding changes.

Removed fabricated standard editions. The EN 1998-1 and DIN 4149 editions previously cited do not exist; governing codes are now named as EN 1998-1:2004+A1:2013 (§4.3.5) and DIN EN 1998-1/NA:2018-10, both recorded as giving no MEP dimensional rules, with DIN 4149:2005-04 recorded as withdrawn.
Removed the wrong EN 1998-1 clause reference; EN 1998-1 Chapter 5 covers concrete buildings, and non-structural elements are §4.3.5.

Corrected seismic_parameters.importance_factors.hospital from 1.6 to 1.5 (FEMA E-74 §5.3.1; ASCE/SEI 7-10 §13.1.3). This alters verdicts wherever the hospital importance factor is consumed; at schema 1.1.0 no SB-001 code path reads it, so no current finding changes.
Set thresholds.duct_area_sqm from null to 0.557 (6 sq ft; FEMA E-74 §6.4.6.1 and App. A §3.9.E.1). At schema 1.1.0 no SB-001 code path reads it, so no current finding changes.
Re-labelled every other threshold as authored calibration or derived arithmetic, with per-threshold provenance. No other value changed.
ruleset_id and schema_version added to the Hermes-generated config.

provenance_summary.statement: BIMGUARD SB-001 is a screening tool whose dimensional thresholds are authored calibration except where marked sourced, and it is not a substitute for design to ASCE/SEI 7-10 §13.6 or EN 1998-1. Sourced: the two component importance factors and the duct area threshold (FEMA E-74), the four brace angle constraints (Hilti Seismic Manual 05/2022), and the two brace spacing values (Hilti Seismic Manual 05/2022, citing NFPA 13 / EN 12845 Annex E). Clearance additions and the base clearance remain authored screening calibration. The pipe diameter threshold is marked unsourced: it is an unverified figure from the same fabricated research pass as the former angle and spacing values, with no sourced replacement found in the sources held.

source.document: FEMA E-74, Reducing the Risks of Nonstructural Earthquake Damage – A Practical Guide, 4th ed., December 2012

importance_factors.hospital.note: Ip = 1.5 for designated seismic systems, including critical nonstructural components in Risk Category IV buildings; 1.0 otherwise. Corrected from 1.6 on 2026-09-13: no Ip of 1.6 exists. The 1.6 in the earlier source is the coefficient in the force cap 1.6·S_DS·Ip·Wp (FEMA E-74 p.5-10), a different quantity.

source.document: FEMA E-74, Reducing the Risks of Nonstructural Earthquake Damage – A Practical Guide, 4th ed., December 2012

importance_factors.standard.note: Ip = 1.0 for components that are not designated seismic systems.

source.document: FEMA E-74, Reducing the Risks of Nonstructural Earthquake Damage – A Practical Guide, 4th ed., December 2012

thresholds.duct_area_sqm.note: E-74 exempts HVAC ducts with cross-sectional area under 6 sq ft (or weighing under 17 lb/ft) where impact is avoided or protected against; bracing is required above that or for ducts carrying hazardous materials. 6 sq ft = 0.557 m²: the metric conversion is BIMGUARD's, as E-74 is US customary throughout and gives no metric equivalent for this value. At schema 1.1.0 no SB-001 code path reads this value.

brace_types.*.spacing_transverse_m.note: Sourced. Replaces the former 1.0, which was not BIMGUARD calibration: it was the same unverified Hermes research pass that produced the fabricated brace angle, with an additional feet-written-as-inches unit corruption -- the same figure, stated once in metres and once (corrupted) in inches by that pass's two invented per-standard entries, survived a min() merge across them. The real value the corrupted figure belongs to is 40 ft (12.19 m), which this source states directly as 12 m. See changelog 1.3.0 and D:/claude-workspace/hilti-seismic/sb001_spacing_investigation.md.

brace_types.*.spacing_longitudinal_m.note: Sourced. Replaces the former 1.5, from the same fabricated Hermes pass as the transverse value, with an extra digit change (the real 80 ft became 60 in before conversion to 1.5 m). The real NFPA 13 value is 80 ft (24.38 m), which this source states directly as 24 m. See changelog 1.3.0 and D:/claude-workspace/hilti-seismic/sb001_spacing_investigation.md.

source.related_reference: FEMA E-74, Reducing the Risks of Nonstructural Earthquake Damage – A Practical Guide, 4th ed., December 2012, Appendix A §3.9.D.9, p. A-13 (PDF p.751)

clearance_rules.base_from_structure_mm.note: Authored. No source. Also the value of brace_types[*].clearance_mm, which the loader applies in preference. FEMA E-74 App. A §3.9.D.9 gives a related rule, horizontal clearance of at least 2/3 the hanger length, but only for unbraced (exempt) piping. No braced-service clearance dimension exists in any source held.

source.document: Unverified Hermes research pass (docs/validation/data/hermes_standards_research_summary.json), same origin as the pre-2026-09-16 brace angle and pre-2026-09-16 brace spacing values
source.related_reference: FEMA E-74, Reducing the Risks of Nonstructural Earthquake Damage – A Practical Guide, 4th ed., December 2012, §6.4.3.1, p.6-238 (PDF p.331)

thresholds.pipe_diameter_mm.note: Not a BIMGUARD authored calibration and not a stated standard value: this is an unverified figure carried over from the same fabricated Hermes research pass that produced the brace angle and brace spacing values (see changelog 1.2.0 and 1.3.0), flagged by the same unit-mirroring signature (EN 63 mm ≈ 2.48 in, close to NFPA's reported ≈2.5 in). Falls within the ASCE 7-10 exemption band FEMA E-74 §6.4.3.1 reports (roughly 1 to 3 in / 25.4-76.2 mm depending on seismic design category and occupancy), but that band does not fix a single threshold, so it does not confirm the value. No document in D:/claude-workspace/hilti-seismic/sources (NFPA 13, UFGS 23 05 48.19, Hilti Seismic Manual) states a pipe-diameter seismic-bracing exemption threshold, so no sourced replacement is available; the value is left at 63.0 pending one and is marked unsourced/placeholder rather than authored.

source.section: Annex A, "Tilt angle – for all bracings"
source.detail: Nominal brace tilt angle 45° ± 15°, side view, stated as the bracing angle on the horizontal level; repeated on the typical application sheets as "brace angle: 45° ± 15°" and used in the worked example as "Assuming α = 45°".
source.upstream: EN 1998-1:2004 §4.3.5 (the manual's design framework; EN 1998-1 itself states no brace angle)

angle_constraints.min_degrees.note: Lower bound of the source's stated 45° ± 15° band (45 - 15). Datum: degrees from horizontal, the same convention the source uses. Replaces the former 40.0, which came from an unverified AI research summary; see changelog 1.2.0. FEMA E-74 contains no brace angle for pipe or duct. A vendor design manual, not a code.

angle_constraints.max_degrees.note: Upper bound of the source's stated 45° ± 15° band (45 + 15). Datum: degrees from horizontal. Replaces the former 65.0, which came from an unverified AI research summary; see changelog 1.2.0. A vendor design manual, not a code.

angle_constraints.ideal_degrees.note: The source's stated nominal angle, not a midpoint computed by BIMGUARD. It is also the midpoint of 30-60 degrees. Replaces the former 52.5, which was the midpoint of the superseded 40-65 range.

source.document: Hilti Seismic Manual – Earthquake-resistant design of MEP supports, MT System (05/2022)
source.section: Annex A, "Tilt angle – for all bracings"

angle_constraints.tolerance_degrees.note: The source's stated tolerance about the 45° nominal (± 15°), not a half-range computed by BIMGUARD. Replaces the former 12.5, which was the half-range of the superseded 40-65 range. The source's separate plan-view limit ("max. 5°" deviation of the brace from the pipe axis) has no field in this schema.

source.related_reference: FEMA E-74, Reducing the Risks of Nonstructural Earthquake Damage – A Practical Guide, 4th ed., December 2012, Appendix A §1.7.C-D, p. A-6 (PDF p.744)

clearance_rules.seismic_zone_addition_mm.note: Authored, no source. E-74 gives relative-displacement design (0.02 × storey height, App. A §1.7.C) and seismic-joint crossings sized by structural analysis (§1.7.D), neither of which adds clearance.

source.related_reference: FEMA E-74, Reducing the Risks of Nonstructural Earthquake Damage – A Practical Guide, 4th ed., December 2012, §5.3.1, p.5-9 (PDF p.85)

clearance_rules.hospital_addition_mm.note: Authored, no source. Hospitals attract stricter requirements (Ip 1.5, certification, post-event function), not larger clearances.

source.related_reference: FEMA E-74, Reducing the Risks of Nonstructural Earthquake Damage – A Practical Guide, 4th ed., December 2012, §2.2.4, p.2-10 (PDF p.22); Appendix A §1.8.D.2-3, p. A-8 (PDF p.746)

clearance_rules.adjacent_system_mm.note: Authored, no source. E-74 §2.2.4 and App. A §1.8.D.2-3 describe service-to-service interaction and require tolerance verification, but give no distance.

CEN. EN 1998-1:2004+A1:2013, Eurocode 8: Design of structures for earthquake resistance – Part 1: General rules, seismic actions and rules for buildings. §4.3.5. Gives no MEP dimensional rules.
DIN. DIN EN 1998-1/NA:2018-10, National Annex – Nationally determined parameters for EN 1998-1. Gives no MEP dimensional rules.

Hilti Corporation (2022). Seismic Manual – Earthquake-resistant design of MEP supports, MT System. Document W4571 EN, 05/2022. NFPA 13, Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems. Not held directly; cited via the Hilti Seismic Manual for the 12 m / 24 m restraint spacing.

CEN. EN 12845, Fixed firefighting systems – Automatic sprinkler systems – Design, installation and maintenance, Annex E. Not held directly; cited via the Hilti Seismic Manual for the 12 m / 24 m restraint spacing.
